claim_versions.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 078 (The three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture.; papers: Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Let 0<s<=1. A sequence of bounded planar pair laws is dominated with subpower loss by two named populations with conditional child rate s. Both populations have polynomial no-strip decay at every fixed positive depth. Original direction bins conditional on both pins are homogeneous on one common subpower-mass finite-test event over simultaneous good-parent fibers. Then uniform trims have conditional direction prefix ball dimension at least s under either pin, hereditary under subpower restrictions retaining the hypotheses.

If P(H|A_j=c)=r_c and a separation restriction retains relative mass v_c inside P(.|H,A_j=c), original uniform conditional direction caps averaged over A in that parent give the actual retained B marginal the same cap multiplied by (r_c v_c)^(-1). A further raw-mass M core multiplies this bound by at most M^(-1).

Inside a depth-j A parent separated subpowerly from B, original homogeneous direction counts at depths j,j+a imply scalar projection counts rho^(-(F_B(j+a)-F_B(j))-o(1)) for the rescaled A child at precision rho^a, for each fixed 0<a<j.
Using the same original homogeneous pair law and actual-marginal core, a two-pin star and the no-strip hypothesis yield F_A prime and F_B prime at least s/2 almost everywhere.

Given F_A(d),F_B(d)>=u d for 0<u<=s on the same pair law, retained marginal transfer and the weighted projection estimate yield F_A prime,F_B prime>=(s+u)/2 almost everywhere; finite iteration tends to s.

The manuscript weighted tagged projection bound with exponent min{1,d,(d+u)/2} follows from the Ren-Wang discrete nice-configuration theorem, including positive product-mass incomplete incidence graphs.

Conditional on the current upstream one-label products, tested prefix caps, prefix capacity floors, and the explicitly assumed no-strip branch, lines 995-1150 provide all directional-bootstrap hypotheses on a common first-pair law and preserve the subsequent scalar direction caps.
The same global floored tree atoms give lambda(Theta_(j+a)|Theta_j)<=rho^(s a-4 delta_mesh-o(1)) at every fixed real parent and increment, without replacing the named population.

Finite simultaneous homogenization and a finite-list refresh on the retained triple give uniform original conditional bins under both pins on one common pair event; pair-only filters leave conditional scalar laws on retained full pairs unchanged.

Prior literature contains two-sided product-graph thin-tube bootstraps and finite-scale robust near-Ahlfors variants; these do not by themselves establish the staged arbitrary dominated conditional-pair interface.

For every delta>0 the three-dimensional Bochner-Riesz multiplier T_delta is bounded on L^3(R^3), as asserted in staged 01-introduction.tex, Theorem thm:bochner-riesz; unverified by this bounded mission.

For all finite nonnegative matrices and normalized nonnegative reference weights, a two-sided degree core at threshold delta>=0 has mass at least the original mass minus 2 delta and surviving row and column masses at least delta times their reference weights. Positive thresholds transfer every original per-fiber event cap to that same core with factor delta^(-1). Averaging row caps inside a positive parent and normalizing retentions r,v gives exactly the cap factor (r v)^(-1), without an inverse parent mass. The nested-tree interpolation exponent loses at most 4 mesh widths.

Averaging row caps inside a positive parent and normalizing retentions r,v gives exactly the cap factor (r v)^(-1), without an inverse parent mass.
